headline: OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said the world should accept some harm from AI in return for its benefits, setting himself apart from rival Anthropic on regulation.
score_reason: Fresh on-record statement by the head of a leading AI lab on how AI should be regulated; read through a relay of the Politico interview, not the Reuters text.
importance_line: Altman's stance affects how lawmakers and the public weigh safety rules, mainly the policy fight between OpenAI and Anthropic, but it is an interview position and no rule has changed.
summary: Politico reports, in an interview for the debut edition of its Decoded series, that OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said "the world should accept some bad things happening" for the benefits of AI and that his company and Anthropic have "a lot of daylight" between their policy views. Altman added that he does not think society should accept "really catastrophic risks", including a serious loss of control over AI.
notes: Original Reuters page blocked (401) and Politico page blocked (403); text read on TradingView, which carries a Benzinga write-up crediting the Politico interview. Reuters headline matches. URL is the page where the text was read.
